title: Operating lease with escalating rent — Juniper Retail
instructions: On January 1, Year 1, Juniper Retail signed a 4-year operating lease for a store. Payments are due at the END of each year. The discount rate is **6%**. Round to whole dollars.

exhibits.title: Payment schedule
exhibits.content:
| Year | Payment (Dec 31) |
|---|---:|
| 1 | 40,000 |
| 2 | 44,000 |
| 3 | 48,000 |
| 4 | 52,000 |

Present value of the payments at 6%: **$158,386**. No initial direct costs or incentives.

rows.label: Interest accretion on the lease liability
ROU asset at December 31
rows.explanation: 158,386 − 36,497 = **121,889**. It's 6,000 below the liability — the accrued rent (46,000 cost − 40,000 paid).

parts.prompt: Which excerpt (paraphrased for study) requires the single straight-line cost for Juniper's lease?

excerpts.text: For a finance lease, a lessee recognizes amortization of the right-of-use asset and interest on the lease liability.
For an operating lease, a lessee recognizes a single lease cost, calculated so that the remaining cost of the lease is allocated over the remaining lease term on a generally straight-line basis.
A lessee classifies a lease as a finance lease if it meets any of five criteria, including transfer of ownership and a lease term for the major part of the asset's remaining economic life.
A lessee may elect not to recognize right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for short-term leases.

parts.explanation: ASC 842-20-25-6 prescribes the single straight-line lease cost for operating leases.
